summary:
# NOTES: The Confounding of Camelia (Anne Douglas Sedgwick, 1899)

Single book, no BOOK headings. Chapters I–XXX (plus THE END). Dedicated "TO 'CHARLIE' AND 'JIMMIE'".

## Characters
- **Camelia Paton** (Célimène): heroine, ~23, only daughter of Sir Charles Paton (dead, adventurous ex-army, yellow curls, "wild" Apollo-like) and Lady Paton. Pale gold hair, gray "sunlit brook" eyes, slim, "Artemis" hands/feet, della Robbia/Madonna look. Gay, selfish, clever, performs for admirers; keen on "personage" status, Japanese prints, Whistler-like, Degas, Outamaro. Calls Perior "Alceste"; he calls her "Célimène", "little pagan", "bandersnatch" reversed, "little scamp", "prig" (she says he's prig).
- **Michael Perior** (Alceste): ~40+, family friend/mentor since Camelia's childhood; ex-editor of the *Friday Review* (weekly leading article). Gray stony eyes, rough gray hair, shaggy, clean-shaven, solid dusty boots, gray-eyed, "uningratiating self-reliance". Lives at the Grange (gray stone house, five miles from Enthorpe, on a hill, yew trees, pansies, irises), with setter dog and cats (Siegfried is Camelia's bull-dog). Irish ancestry (Irish ancestress). Idealist, scorns "second-best", sociologist of model cottages (Morris-free, bath-tubs, Pears' soap, tenant "Dirt is the root of all evil"). Killed foxes at Mandelly Woods; tutors village boys; Job Masters works in his laboratory (infusoria, microscope). Father ruined in lawsuit, jilted at 23; mother Mrs. Perior died. Fond of Lady Paton ("Angelica"), calls her Angelica? (Lady Paton calls him Michael.)
- **Lady Paton** (Angelica, "Aunt Angelica"): thin, graceful, black mourning, white caps, round child-like eyes, "hare under a bramble"; timid, sweet, dull, knits; calls Camelia "darling"; family's dutiful wife. Eight-daughter Fairleigh baronet's daughter (Miss Fairleigh before marriage).
- **Mary Fairleigh**: niece (daughter of Maurice Fairleigh & nursery governess Miss Hockey), flaxen hair, short nose, clumsy mouth, "lacteal dulness", ugly, stolid. Lives at Enthorpe since age 16 (mother Angelica/Mrs. Fairleigh died). Dutiful, reads aloud, Sunday-school, Kitty Brown. Secretly loves Perior. Has consumption (father died of it; cough, blood). Dies in spring, having confessed to Camelia; forgives her; tells Perior "You will marry Camelia." Mary's last words: "I love you" (to Camelia) and "I win—where Camelia failed!"
- **Mrs. Fox-Darriel** (Frances): Camelia's smart friend, artificial, stayless, bangles/lorgnettes, husband Hon. Charlie (impecunious); calls Perior "vial of wrath"/"provincial Diogenes"; wants Camelia to marry rich Sir Arthur; later says "Endymion stooped to Selena" and Latmos.
- **Sir Arthur Henge**: rich, young (30+), handsome, serious, Factory Bill sponsor, Tory-liberal, religious; brown dog-like eyes; calls Camelia "my laughing child". Engaged to Camelia; she breaks it off.
- **Lady Henge**: stately, conscientious, composer of "Thalassa" (symphonic poem, sea/seasick); Perior calls it "very bad". Wanted Lady Elizabeth (Duchess of Amshire's daughter) for son.
- **Mr. Rodrigg**: iron-gray, middle-aged politician, ruddy, broad-tipped nose ("plebeian", Camelia dislikes); opposes Factory Bill; "bull-dog"; Camelia flirts; he storms in and exposes engagement; calls her "Miss Paton"; says "Allow me to congratulate you". Camelia says "Odious vulgarian".
- **Mrs. Jedsley**: old rector's widow, stout, choleric red eyebrows, frank; "cow in the landscape" remark; loves Camelia grudgingly.
- **Lady Haversham**: county magnate; "drum-like" manner; Lord Haversham (axes, cottages rents).
- **Mrs. Grier**: musical, charitable, long nose, son at Oxford; almshouses, Copley children.
- **Gwendolen Holt**, **Sir Harry**, **Mr. Merriman**, **Lady Tramley** (Jack Tramley's wife, friend, "season of penance"), the poet with virile poems. Visitors at Enthorpe.
- **Mary's servants/others**: Lane (old butler at Grange), Grant (Camelia's maid), Jane Hicks (dying paralysed farm girl; Camelia visited once), Mrs. Brown, Mrs. Dawkins, Coles (cottage tenants), Mappuck girls (tennis), Mr. Ballenden (atheist writer), Mr. Dobson (report), Arthur Henge's sister none. Henge's letter "Arthur" wrote to Perior; Perior's old fag at Eton: Arthur Henge.

## Places
Clievesbury (village, Blankshire); Enthorpe Lodge (Patons' house, morning room, drawing-room with Steinway, library, copper-beech tree, magnolia window); the Grange (Perior's house, library, laboratory top floor, the Manor); Mandelly Woods; the Common; Copley (village); Manor Farm; churchyard; Haversham; Laversley Castle (Mrs F-D's dream); Homburg; Florence; Paris (Rue de la Paix); Davos-Platz (Maurice died); India (Sir Charles' posts); Italy (Perior's trip).

## Plot in order
**Ch I**: Camelia returns after second London season. Clievesbury gossip: "spoiled"; Mrs. Jedsley denounces her; Sir Charles's vanity. Lady Haversham tries to snub her; Camelia's cool eyes make her cows.
**Ch II**: Morning room, Camelia waits for Perior, with Mrs. Fox-Darriel. Camelia's stayless gowns (Paris), "I don't think it looks alive." Perior arrives late: "Well, Célimène." "Well, Alceste."
**Ch III**: Perior's first visit; Greek lessons; Camelia's Whistler portrait "portrait of a smile"; Lord/Henge letter about Factory Bill, "Samson", Rodrigg "Philistine"; Perior's sense of Camelia's "femme bibelot"; Camelia mocks Mary as "raisinless milk pudding".
**Ch IV**: Lady Paton, Mary (headache, tennis with Mappuck girls); Perior's cottages/pure experiment; "Calvinist" joke; Perior: "Dirt is the root of all evil". Camelia: "neighbor's corns".
**Ch V**: Perior's backstory (father's lawsuit, jilted, journalism, mother's death). Camelia as child; her lying at 18; Mary's coming at 16; Perior's promise never to be hurt. Foxes shot; Burns-like poacher's son at Oxford; Henge letter about Lady Henge.
**Ch VI**: Camelia & Mrs F-D; Henge marriage talk; "Decide"; Camelia "Lady Henge comes too"; Mrs F-D sees Camelia walk with Perior on lawn; Perior switches calf with whip.
**Ch VII**: Tea with Mrs Jedsley; Camelia's Japanese flower arrangement; Mary's Beethoven sonata flushes; Perior says Lady Henge's music "very bad" later; Camelia's rose for Mrs J.
**Ch VIII**: Henges arrive (Monday). Lady Henge's "Thalassa" performed. Perior: "I think it is very bad." Camelia & Arthur in garden: she lies, claims not laughing; "Don't be insincere, dearest." Moonlight. Camelia & Mary in her room: Mary wants to say something, Camelia says "No, you little goose".
**Ch IX**: Camelia flirts; Arthur talks Factory Bill; Rodrigg "fond of me"; she claims she refused Rodrigg; Perior comes; she wheedles him to morning-room.
**Ch X**: Quarrel: Perior "You lied... to Arthur"; Camelia cries: "It is false"; "You are a prig"; he refuses lunch.
**Ch XI**: Guests leave; Rodrigg arrives; Lady Henge preaches to Rodrigg; Camelia argues bill with him; Perior warns "bribing"; Camelia says she "pinched" Rodrigg.
**Ch XII**: Thursday ride; Camelia engineers Perior to stay; sends Mary away to Mrs Grier's almshouses with a lie (headache); Mary cries; Perior talks with Camelia; "Mary likes curates"; tea under copper-beech; Revue des Deux Mondes; Agamemnon.
**Ch XIII**: Perior meets Mary returning; she cries; he learns Camelia lied; Mary says "She did not know I was going with you"; Mary weeps in room.
**Ch XIV**: Perior confronts Camelia on lawn; she confesses fully (wanted to read him Revue; let Mary think he preferred her); Perior: "You are breaking my heart"; "I do not love you"-ish; she says "You'd rather stay with me."
**Ch XV**: Camelia waits; letters ("Try to be good without me"); Mrs F-D comments "Laversley"; Camelia closes hand; accepts Arthur.
**Ch XVI**: Camelia accepts Arthur (in library, Lady Henge playing epithalamium). She sends note to Perior: "I am very unhappy." Camelia dances (pavane, gavotte, courante) in white dress; Perior kisses her; "Too enchanting... Forgive me." "I love you enough to kiss you... go away."
**Ch XVII**: Rodrigg bursts in: "Lady Henge tells me you accepted her son." Camelia: "Yes, Mr. Rodrigg, I did." Rodrigg leaves. Camelia to Perior: "I love you." Perior: "By Heaven I don't."
**Ch XVIII**: Perior's night of disgust; Arthur comes to Grange; breaks engagement (Camelia said "I made a mistake... unworthy"); Perior tells Arthur she is "false, voraciously selfish, hard as a stone"; Arthur leaves for London. Camelia comes to Grange; Perior: "I do not love you... I will not marry you"; she clings; "Will you kiss me good-bye?"
**Ch XIX**: Mrs F-D: "Did you break... shall I?" Camelia: "I don't love him. Please go, Frances." Mrs F-D leaves for the Dormers. Lady Paton knocks; Camelia refuses.
**Ch XX**: Mrs Jedsley's visit to Lady Paton; her theory Camelia fond of Perior; Mrs Jedsley & Mary walk; Mary's fear of being discovered; Mary cries at churchyard lane.
**Ch XXI**: Camelia's gloom; Lady Paton's lament; Camelia's resolve to be good; plans model cottages; visits Lady Tramley in London; Lady Tramley says Perior back from Continent fighting bill.
**Ch XXII**: Camelia reads sociology; Camelia reads Friday Review article by Perior; Mary sees; Camelia snaps "You look like a spy!"; Mary sobs; apology next day.
**Ch XXIII**: Bill defeated (late January); Mrs Jedsley sneers; Camelia rides, meets Perior on common; they make peace; Camelia tells him she's building cottages; Mary's hatred grows.
**Ch XXIV**: Jane Hicks dies with Camelia's hand; Perior, Camelia, Mary walk; Mary's secrets (dying, loves Perior); Mary confronts Camelia: "I love him... you took him from me"; Mary strikes/blames Camelia: "I hate you."
**Ch XXV**: Camelia gallops to the Grange, tells Perior Mary is dying and loves him; asks him to marry Mary; he refuses ("I could not act such a lie").
**Ch XXVI**: Camelia returns; Mary followed her; accuses her; Camelia says she wanted Perior to marry Mary; Mary strikes her cheek; Camelia summons help.
**Ch XXVII**: Perior at Enthorpe; Lady Paton reports Mary dying; Camelia sits by Mary; Mary says "Camelia, I am sorry." Camelia confesses love for Perior; Mary: "But I love you, Camelia."
**Ch XXVIII**: Mary asks Perior to visit; Mary tells Perior to marry Camelia ("I win—where Camelia failed!"); Mary dies after Perior kisses her.
**Ch XXIX**: Weeks later; Perior admits he always loved Camelia; Camelia confesses her long wrongs to Mary; "Don't shut yourself in." Lovers quietly; Camelia's teasing; cabbages/orchids.
**Ch XXX**: Next October. Mrs. Fox-Darriel visits (staying with the Lambournes, 20 miles off); Camelia says she is marrying Perior ("Console yourself, Frances"); "Endymion stooped to Selena"; Latmos. Camelia & Perior in garden at dusk; one star; "Quite good enough for me... I am getting tired of your conscience, Camelia." THE END.

## Key quoted phrases
"Well, Célimène." / "Well, Alceste."; "portrait of a smile"; "You are breaking my heart"; "By Heaven I don't"; "I love you enough to kiss you"; "Yes, Mr. Rodrigg, I did"; "You look like a spy!"; "I win—where Camelia failed!"; "I love you"; "I am getting tired of your conscience, Camelia."
